During peak rush hour on a busy metro line, an Express metro train of length 240 meters running at 72 km/h approaches a Local metro train of length 160 meters moving on a parallel track at 36 km/h in the same direction. From the instant the front of the Express train aligns with the rear of the Local train, how much time (in seconds) will it take for the Express train to completely overtake the Local train?

Step-by-Step Solution: 1) Total Distance to clear = Length of Express Train + Length of Local Train = 240 m + 160 m = 400 m. 2) Relative Speed (since both move in the same direction) = Speed of Express - Speed of Local = 72 km/h - 36 km/h = 36 km/h. 3) Convert Relative Speed to m/s: 36 * (5/18) = 10 m/s. 4) Time required = Total Distance / Relative Speed = 400 m / 10 m/s = 40 seconds. Burra Trick (Speed Math): Whenever relative speed is a multiple of 18 km/h, convert instantly by multiplying the multiple by 5 m/s. Here, 72 - 36 = 36 km/h = 2 * 18 km/h -> 2 * 5 = 10 m/s. Total distance = 240 + 160 = 400 m. Mental calculation: 400 / 10 = 40 seconds!

A metro commuter walks up an ascending escalator and counts 40 steps to reach the top platform in 30 seconds. If the escalator stops during a maintenance drill and he walks up at the exact same speed, he takes 60 steps. How many total visible steps does the escalator have?

Let escalator speed = e steps/sec, commuter walking speed = c steps/sec.
When stationary, total steps N = 60 steps.
In moving case: Commuter takes 40 steps in 30 s => c = 40 / 30 = 4/3 steps/sec.
Since total stationary steps = 60, time to walk stationary = 60 / (4/3) = 45 seconds.
Escalator saved 15 seconds (45s down to 30s).
Escalator contributes: (60 / 45) * 30 = 40 steps of the total.
Total visible escalator steps = 40 (commuter) + 80 (escalator assist) = 120 steps.
Burra Trick: When speeds are constant, (Steps_moving / Time_moving) = c, giving total steps N = (Steps_walking * Total_time_ratio) = 120 steps!

During evening rush hour, two Hyderabad Metro trains travel on parallel tracks in opposite directions. Train A is 200 meters long and travels at a speed of 60 km/h. Train B is 250 meters long. If the two trains pass each other completely in 15 seconds, what is the speed of Train B in km/h?

Step 1: Calculate the total distance to be covered for the trains to cross each other completely: Distance = Length of Train A + Length of Train B = 200 m + 250 m = 450 m. Step 2: Calculate the relative speed in m/s: Relative Speed = Total Distance / Time = 450 m / 15 s = 30 m/s. Step 3: Convert the relative speed to km/h: 30 * (18 / 5) = 108 km/h. Step 4: Since the trains move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = Speed_A + Speed_B. Therefore, 108 = 60 + Speed_B => Speed_B = 108 - 60 = 48 km/h. BURRA TRICK: Speed_B = [(L1 + L2) / Time] * 3.6 - Speed_A = (450 / 15) * 3.6 - 60 = 30 * 3.6 - 60 = 108 - 60 = 48 km/h.
